instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are NINE questions in this paper.

sub_questions.text: State zeroth law of thermodynamics and explain its utility in measuring temperature.
Explain the difference between microscopic and macroscopic form of energy. Give examples.
Write down the expressions for 'efficiency of heat engines', 'COP of refrigerator' and 'COP of heat pump' if all of them are operating between the same heat reservoirs.
How do the values of $\int_1^2 \frac{\delta Q}{T}$ compare for a reversible and irreversible processes between the same end states?
Define 'availability'. Which of the two sources of energy viz., 'potential energy' and 'thermal energy' source possesses higher value of availability?
Why there is no constant temperature line in the wet region of Mollier diagram? Explain.

From the relationships given below, identify the relationship which is consequence of Helmholtz function
$du = TdS - pdv$
$dg = -SdT + Vdp$
$dh = TdS + Vdp$
$da = -SdT - pdv$
Explain the difference between air-standard cycle and standard air-fuel cycle.
Which four processes constitute the simple ideal Rankine cycle? Sketch the cycle on T-S diagram.
Define absolute and relative humidity and give the relation between them.
Does satisfying the first law of thermodynamics ensure that process will actually take place? Justify your answer by at least two examples.

Air enters adiabatic gas turbine at $1000\text{ kPa}$ and $500^\circ\text{C}$ and leaves it at $100\text{ kPa}$ and $150^\circ\text{C}$. The entry of air is through $0.2\text{ m}^2$ opening with an average velocity of $40\text{ m/s}$ and exhausts through $1\text{ m}^2$ opening. Determine the mass flow rate of air through the turbine and the power produced by the turbine.

Show that there exists a property of a closed system such that change in its value is equal to $\int_1^2 \frac{\delta Q}{T}$ for a reversible process undergone by the system between state '1' and '2'.

A piston cylinder device contains $1.2\text{ kg}$ of nitrogen gas at $120\text{ kPa}$ and $300\text{ K}$. The gas is now compressed slowly in a polytropic process during which $pv^{1.3} = c$. The process is stopped when the volume becomes half the original volume. Determine the change in entropy of nitrogen.
Sketch the Carnot cycle for heat engine on a $p-v$ plane. Using this diagram, find out an expression for the thermal efficiency of the cycle.

A household refrigerator with a COP of 1.2 removes heat from refrigerated space at the rate of $60\text{ kJ/min}$. Calculate (i) the electric power consumed by the refrigerator, (ii) heat transfer to the kitchen air and (iii) the higher temperature of the cycle if the average temperature in the refrigerator is $-20^\circ\text{C}$.

Define the following:
(i) Compressed liquid
(ii) Saturated liquid
(iii) Superheated vapour
(iv) Saturated vapour

A mass of wet steam at a temperature of $165^\circ\text{C}$ with dryness fraction 0.80 is expanded to a pressure of 3 bar in such a way that quality remains the same. Isobaric heating is then adopted till the degree of superheat becomes $66.5^\circ\text{C}$. Find the enthalpy and entropy changes during the two processes. Draw the T-S and H-S diagrams.
Name the basic ideal cycle for modern gas turbine and designate the different processes which constitute the cycle. Find out an expression for its thermal efficiency.

A reciprocating gasoline engine has a volumetric compression ratio of 8. The pressure and temperature of air before the compression begins are $85\text{ kPa}$ and $280\text{ K}$. The combustion generates peak pressure of $6500\text{ kPa}$. Find the peak temperature, the energy added by combustion process and exhaust temperature.
Explain the effect of reheat on (i) specific output, (ii) cycle efficiency, (iii) steam rate and (iv) heat rate of a steam power plant.

Steam enters a turbine at $40\text{ bar}$ and $350^\circ\text{C}$, it expands in the turbine until it is dry and saturated and then it is reheated to $350^\circ\text{C}$. The condenser pressure is 0.04 bar. Calculate the work output and cycle efficiency assuming isentropic expansion and neglecting pump work. Also estimate the steam flow rate for an output of $100\text{ MW}$.

State and explain Dalton's law of additive pressure and Amagat's law of additive volume for mixture of ideal gases. Also show that partial pressure fraction and volume fraction are equal to mole fraction.

A mixture consists of $8\text{ kmol}$ of $\text{H}_2$ and $2\text{ kmol}$ of $\text{N}_2$. Calculate the mass of each gas and apparent gas constant of the mixture. Also calculate the density and volume of the mixture at $100\text{ kPa}$ and $300\text{ K}$.
Explain the meaning of (i) dry-bulb temperature, (ii) wet-bulb temperature, (iii) dew point and (iv) adiabatic saturation temperature.

The air in a room has a dry-bulb temperature of $25^\circ\text{C}$ and wet-bulb temperature of $15^\circ\text{C}$. Assuming a pressure of $100\text{ kPa}$, determine (i) specific humidity, (ii) relative humidity and (iii) dew point.
